name: Alfalfa / Lucerne (perennial hay)

temperate_high_input.notes: US Midwest dormant hay alfalfa (3-4 cuts/yr DM equivalent; USDA NASS Iowa).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: NSW Riverina irrigated/dryland pasture phase lucerne (NSW DPIRD).

notes: Deep-rooted perennial legume (dry-matter hay yield across 3-4 cuts/yr) building deep SOC, subsoil structure, and supplying 150-200 kg N/ha credit for subsequent corn/wheat.

name: Barley

maritime_europe.notes: Beauce France winter/spring malting barley (Agreste/ARVALIS mean ~7.1 t/ha).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Southern Australia winter-sown feed/malting barley (ABARES/GRDC Riverina ~3.2 t/ha).

temperate_high_input.notes: US Upper Midwest spring malting barley (USDA NASS).

notes: Lower-water, salt- and alkali-tolerant rabi cereal for south-west Punjab (Bathinda, Fazilka, Muktsar). Recommended PAU varieties include DWRB 123 (malt) and PL 891. Matures 10-15 days earlier than wheat, reliably escaping late March terminal heat spikes; needs only 2-3 irrigations compared to 4-5 for wheat.

name: Basmati rice
notes: Later transplanting (July) uses more monsoon rain; export market price, no MSP.

name: Berseem (Egyptian clover, fodder)
notes: King of rabi fodders in Punjab dairy farming (varieties BL 42, BL 43, BL 10). Yields 5-6 succulent cuts from November through May; often mixed with Chinese sarson or oats in the first cutting for early bulk. Exceptionally high biological nitrogen fixation leaves substantial residual N, rejuvenating depleted rice-wheat soils; valid only when FarmConstraints.has_livestock is active.

name: Brachiaria / Urochloa (tropical cover)
notes: Deep-rooting tropical Sistema Santa Fe / plantio direto mulch grass generating 7-10 t/ha straw biomass over dry season in Brazil Cerrado (EMBRAPA).
sources: EMBRAPA Sistema Plantio Direto / Santa Fe

name: Cassava (mandioca)
notes: Ultra-drought-tolerant tropical carbohydrate staple yielding on acidic, low-fertility soils.

name: Chickpea (gram)
notes: Rainfed-capable rabi legume; suits lighter soils of south-west Punjab.

name: Common bean (dry bean / rajma)

tropical_highland.notes: Kenya Nakuru Rosecoco/Nyota bimodal bush bean (KNBS/KALRO ~1.0 t/ha).

notes: Core pulse for smallholder food security and dietary protein in sub-humid to semi-arid bimodal systems (Kenya Machakos golden field: short rains Oct-Dec and long rains Mar-May; also grown as Rajma in northern India). Bush varieties mature rapidly in 75-90 days, fitting tightly into intercropping with maize or sorghum. Fixes 35-50 kg N/ha via symbiotic Rhizobium leguminosarum bv. phaseoli, reducing synthetic N needs for successor cereals. Extremely sensitive to waterlogging (root rot / Rhizoctonia) and floral heat abortion above 30°C.
sources: KALRO / CIAT Common Bean Production Guide for Eastern Africa

name: Cotton

tropical_high_input.notes: Mato Grosso Cerrado high-input cotton (seed-cotton ~4.2 t/ha, ~1.75 t/ha lint; IMEA/CONAB).

notes: South-west Punjab (Bathinda, Mansa, Fazilka). Sown late April-May, so it overlaps the zaid slot (TASK-O01b: model cotton as occupying zaid+kharif). Yield is seed cotton.

name: Crimson Clover / Hairy Vetch (N cover)
notes: Temperate overwintering legume cover crop (or autumn catch-crop in EU) supplying 80-110 kg N/ha biologically fixed nitrogen to spring maize.

name: Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata, green manure)
notes: Pre-kharif zaid green manure sown late April to early May and incorporated at 45-50 days before succulent stems lignify. Adds 20-25 t/ha fresh green biomass (~4-5 t/ha dry residue), supplying ~80-100 kg N/ha to succeeding puddled or DSR rice. Excellent for improving soil aggregation, water retention, and buffering sodicity/alkalinity in Punjab soils.
sources: PAU Package of Practices Kharif (green manuring)

name: Faba Bean (fevrole)

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Riverina NSW alkaline clay faba bean (GRDC/ABARES).

notes: High N-fixing cool-season legume tolerating heavier wet/clay soils better than chickpea or field pea.

name: Field Pea (dry pea)

maritime_europe.notes: France spring/winter proteaginous field pea (pois proteagineux; Agreste/Terres Inovia ~3.5 t/ha).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Southern Australia winter-sown dun/kaspa field pea (GRDC/ABARES).

notes: Cool-season N-fixing pulse break crop improving first-wheat yields via Rhizobium credit and disease break.

name: Groundnut (Moongphali)
notes: High-value Kharif oilseed-legume suited to well-drained sandy loam and loamy sand soils across Punjab (SG 99, TG 37A), Bundelkhand, Gujarat, and Andhra Pradesh. Symbiotic Rhizobium fixes 50-80 kg N/ha while requiring 65% less water than puddled rice.

name: Lentil (masur)
notes: Low-water rabi pulse ideally suited for rainfed, sub-montane Kandi tracts (Hoshiarpur, Ropar, Gurdaspur) and lighter well-drained soils of Punjab (varieties LL 699, LL 931). Requires only 1-2 irrigations (saving >250 mm water vs wheat) and matures by mid-March, completely evading late heat stress. Leaves 25-30 kg/ha residual N; highly susceptible to waterlogging and collar rot if over-irrigated.

name: Lupin (narrow-leafed / white)

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Southern Australia narrow-leafed lupin on acidic sandy loams (ABARES/GRDC Riverina ~1.6 t/ha).

notes: Deep-taproot acid-soil pulse fixing ~90 kg N/ha and unlocking soil P via proteoid cluster roots.

name: Maize (kharif)

temperate_high_input.notes: US Midwest 105-115 CRM dent hybrid (USDA NASS Story County IA 5-yr mean ~12.35 t/ha).

maritime_europe.notes: France Beauce FAO 300-450 grain maize (Agreste/ARVALIS mean ~9.5 t/ha).

tropical_high_input.notes: Brazil Cerrado safrinha second-crop hybrid after soybean (CONAB/IMEA Mato Grosso ~6.5 t/ha).

tropical_highland.notes: East Africa highland hybrid H614/H6213 (KNBS/KALRO Nakuru County ~2.6-3.0 t/ha).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Irrigated Riverina summer grain maize (NSW DPIRD).

notes: Main water-saving alternative to kharif rice in Punjab. Sensitive to waterlogging during monsoon; avoid low-lying fields. Spring maize is NOT water-saving.

name: Mung bean (moong)
notes: Summer (zaid) moong fits the April-June gap between wheat and rice; residue incorporation adds N for the next crop.
sources: PAU Package of Practices Kharif (summer moong)

name: Mustard / rapeseed
notes: Low-water rabi alternative; brassica break crop reduces cereal disease carry-over.

name: Oats

temperate_high_input.notes: US Midwest spring oats nurse/grain crop (USDA NASS Iowa ~85 bu/ac = 3.05 t/ha).

notes: Tolerates lower pH (down to 5.0) than wheat/barley and serves as an oat-clover nurse crop.

name: Pearl millet (bajra)
notes: Highest heat- and drought-tolerant cereal in the database; perfectly suited to light, sandy loam and low-fertility soils of south-west Punjab (PCB 165, FBC 16). C4 photosynthesis maintains biomass accumulation at ambient temperatures exceeding 40°C; short duration (75-85 days) allows drought escape. Dual-purpose grain and high-biomass nutritious dry stover.

name: Pigeon pea (arhar / tur)
notes: Deep-rooted, drought-tolerant pulse. In Punjab, extra-short duration varieties (AL 882, PAU 881, ~140 d) sown mid-May mature in time for timely November wheat sowing, offering an effective escape from the rice mono-cropping trap. Powerful taproot (up to 2 m) breaks hard subsoil plough pans, improves percolation, and fixes atmospheric nitrogen. Essential crop for the Machakos Kenya golden field, commonly intercropped with maize.

name: Potato (autumn)

maritime_europe.notes: NW Europe maincrop ware/starch potato (Agreste France ~45 t/ha).

temperate_high_input.notes: North America irrigated processing potato (USDA NASS).

tropical_highland.notes: Kenya Shangi / Dutch Robijn highland rainfed potato (KNBS/KALRO Nakuru ~13.5 t/ha).

notes: Sown Oct, harvested Jan; allows a following spring crop. High-value, high input, volatile prices.

name: Rapeseed / Canola

maritime_europe.notes: Beauce France winter colza (Agreste/Terres Inovia ~3.5 t/ha).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Riverina NSW spring-habit Clearfield/TT canola (ABARES/GRDC ~2.1 t/ha).

notes: High-value Brassica break crop interrupting cereal take-all and eyespot disease cycles.

name: Rice (direct-seeded, DSR)
notes: No puddling: saves ~15-25% irrigation water, less labour; weed control critical. Calibrate separately from puddled rice (TASK-M03).

name: Rice (temperate japonica, flooded/AWD)

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Murrumbidgee/Riverina irrigated japonica medium-grain rice (NSW DPIRD).

maritime_europe.notes: Camargue/Po Valley Mediterranean japonica paddy rice.

notes: Temperate-photoperiod japonica paddy rice for warm temperate deltas and Murray-Murrumbidgee irrigation.

name: Rice (puddled, transplanted)
notes: Punjab baseline kharif crop. Transplanting legally delayed to mid-June (Punjab Preservation of Subsoil Water Act 2009). Short-duration PR-126 ~ lower end of duration.
sources: Punjab Preservation of Subsoil Water Act 2009

name: Rice (Short-Duration PR-126)
notes: PAU flagship short-duration paddy variety PR-126 (matures in 93 days after transplanting / 123 days seed-to-seed vs 155 days for Pusa-44). Harvested by early October, opening a 25-30 day burn-free turnaround window before November wheat sowing with Happy Seeder while cutting irrigation demand by ~25% and retaining full FCI MSP procurement.
sources: Punjab Preservation of Subsoil Water Act 2009

name: Upland Rice (aerobic tropical)

tropical_high_input.notes: Brazil Cerrado terras altas BRS Esmeralda/Sertaneja upland rice (CONAB/EMBRAPA).

tropical_highland.notes: East Africa NERICA upland aerobic rice (AfricaRice/KALRO).

notes: Non-flooded aerobic rice adapted to acidic tropical Oxisols and Cerrado/NERICA rainfed systems.

name: Winter Cereal Rye (cover / grain)
notes: Extreme winter-hardy cereal cover crop scavenging 30-55 kg residual NO3-N/ha over winter and suppressing erosion/weeds before spring soybean or maize (USDA-SARE / Midwest Cover Crops Council).

name: Sorghum (jowar / chari)

tropical_high_input.notes: Brazil Cerrado safrinha grain sorghum (CONAB MT).

notes: Drought-resilient Kharif coarse cereal across semi-arid India (Bundelkhand, Deccan plateau; hybrids CSH 16, CSV 27) and dual-purpose grain/fodder crop in North-West India. Dense root system extracts subsoil water under severe moisture stress.
sources: DES Ministry of Agriculture District Yield Statistics

name: Soybean

temperate_high_input.notes: US Midwest Maturity Group II-III soybean (USDA NASS Story County IA ~4.0 t/ha).

tropical_high_input.notes: Brazil Cerrado MG 6-8 safra soybean (IBGE/CONAB Sorriso MT 5-yr mean ~3.60 t/ha).

notes: Major Kharif oilseed-legume across central and peninsular India (Vidarbha, Malwa, Bundelkhand; varieties JS 20-34, JS 95-60, SL 958). Requires well-drained soils (sensitive to prolonged monsoon waterlogging); supplies a 40-50 kg N/ha biological nitrogen credit to succeeding Rabi wheat, chickpea, or mustard.
sources: DES Ministry of Agriculture District Yield Statistics

name: Sugar Beet

maritime_europe.notes: France Beauce/Picardie betterave sucriere (~82 t/ha fresh roots ~16-18% sugar; Agreste/ITB).

temperate_high_input.notes: US Red River Valley/Plains sugar beet (USDA NASS).

notes: Deep-rooting spring-sown industrial root crop requiring >=3 year break for beet cyst nematode suppression.

name: Sunflower

temperate_high_input.notes: US Great Plains oilseed sunflower (USDA NASS).

notes: High-value spring oilseed (40-42% edible oil) cultivated widely across Punjab (hybrids PSH 1962, PSH 2080) sown late January-February after potato, rice, or toria. Its vigorous taproot penetrates 1.5-2.0 m, actively scavenging subsoil moisture and residual nitrate leached from previous heavy-feeder crops. Requires 4-6 irrigations (350-500 mm); critical stages are buttoning and flowering. Sown before peak summer heat and harvested by mid-May, creating a lucrative bridge crop ahead of kharif maize or DSR. Requires pollinator visits (honeybees) for seed set; avoid rotating consecutively with mustard or sunflower due to Sclerotinia sclerotiorum stalk and head rot.
sources: PAU Package of Practices for Crops of Punjab (Rabi / Spring)

name: Sweet Potato

tropical_highland.notes: East Africa orange-fleshed vitamin-A biofortified sweet potato (CIP/KALRO).

notes: Fast-canopy tropical root crop offering rapid ground cover against intense monsoon erosion.

name: Triticale

maritime_europe.notes: France winter triticale for feed/forage on lighter soils (Agreste).

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Australia dual-purpose spring triticale on acidic sandy loams.

notes: Wheat-rye hybrid combining rye's acid-soil/drought tolerance with higher grain yield.

name: Blackgram (Urad / Mash)
notes: Short-duration pulse (Mash 114, Mash 1008 in Punjab; ADT 5 in Cauvery Delta rice-fallows; Bundelkhand Kharif pulse). Fits both Kharif rainfed uplands and Zaid/rice-fallow windows, fixing ~55 kg N/ha and eligible for NAFED PSS procurement.

name: Wheat

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Southern Australia winter-sown spring wheat (ABARES/GRDC Riverina NSW ~3.0 t/ha).

tropical_highland.notes: Kenya Rift Valley highland spring wheat (KNBS/KALRO Nakuru).

notes: Terminal heat in March (grain fill) is the key climate risk in Punjab. Timely sowing early-mid November; Happy/Super Seeder allows sowing into rice residue.

name: Spring Wheat

mediterranean_dryland.notes: Riverina NSW autumn-sown spring-habit bread wheat (ABARES/GRDC mean ~3.0 t/ha).

temperate_high_input.notes: US Northern Plains/Midwest spring wheat (USDA NASS).

tropical_highland.notes: Kenya Nakuru Rift Valley highland wheat (KNBS/KALRO ~2.8 t/ha).

notes: Non-vernalizing spring-habit bread wheat sown in spring in high-latitude continental zones or autumn in mild Mediterranean/highland systems.

name: Winter Wheat

maritime_europe.notes: France Beauce winter soft wheat (ble tendre d'hiver; Agreste/ARVALIS 5-yr mean ~7.3 t/ha).

temperate_high_input.notes: US Midwest/Plains hard/soft winter wheat (USDA NASS).

notes: Autumn-sown vernalizing wheat entering winter dormancy below 2 C and tolerating frost down to -20 C when hardened.
